name: Freya Petrov

opening.speaker: interviewer
opening.text: I am from the Work Futures Panel, an independent research group with no ties to employers, AI companies, unions, parties or government. Your answers are confidential. What does a normal day at your accounting firm look like?

opening.speaker: persona
opening.text: The pool-maintenance contractor sends service dates and chemical invoices in separate exports, and I match them before preparing its accounts and tax return. After years at this level I can usually spot the same filter being billed twice, which I enjoy; the part I hate is calling for a signed job sheet when the contractor has already sent the customer an invoice. I am 58, with a bachelor's degree and a professional accountancy qualification, an experienced mid-level accountant with ordinary rather than exceptional skill. I use AI every day to group a draft exception list, then check the signed job sheet and bank payment myself.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: AI Plateau. Picture this. AI turns out to be mostly hype. It automates some routine tasks and saves a bit of time here and there, but nothing radical changes. Jobs, pay and prices carry on much as they would have anyway.

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: If AI remains a small helper, the exception list will still get me to the doubled filter quickly. It will not decide whether the work was done.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: If this happened, what would you say about it at work, to friends, or online?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I would tell the team to keep the signed service sheet with each disputed invoice. I would tell the contractor which filter charge I removed and why.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: And just between us, off the record, what do you really think it means for you?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: My pay is around the usual rate for an accountant at this level, and my partner Cal and I have five months of expenses saved. Our grown children live elsewhere, our regular home-loan and food bills fit our two wages, and some accounting firms are nearby if one actually posts an opening.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: What would you actually do, starting now and in the first year after it arrives? Be as specific as you can.

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I would keep preparing the paid maintenance accounts and use my approved daily AI list with a signed-sheet check. I would ask my manager Rosa to test an automatic duplicate-filter match on a paid closed month, using the known service sheets; only after it passes and she approves the live change in writing would I use it, otherwise I would keep the current paid process.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: How does it feel, picturing that?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I feel calm about this limited picture. The filter either went in the pool or it did not; the screen cannot make it true.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: Why a closed month?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: We know which service calls were cancelled, so we can count false matches. I would not let a live customer invoice be the test.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: What is the reserve for?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: Five months gives us time if a wage stops. I would not call those existing savings a new investment or a retirement income.

say: I would keep a **signed service sheet** behind disputed charges.
I would explain the **double filter charge** to the contractor.
think: Our **five-month reserve** and two wages cover the current home loan and ordinary household bills.
Some nearby firms offer **possibilities**, not guaranteed vacancies.
do: Keep **paid maintenance accounts** and check approved AI exceptions against signed sheets.
Automate **duplicate-filter matching** only after paid closed-month proof and Rosa's written live approval; otherwise retain the process.
feel: I feel **calm** about a small technology change.
S0.quote: The filter either went in the pool or it did not; the screen cannot make it true.
fieldNote: Daily AI grouping remains a **draft aid** checked against signed service sheets and bank payments.
The automatic match needs **paid historical proof** and written approval, with current paid work as the failure fallback.

steps.text: Keep paid maintenance returns and check approved exceptions against signed service sheets
Automate filter matching only after paid closed-month test passes and Rosa approves live use in writing

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: Steady Disruption. Now picture this. AI brings strong change, but not a revolution. Over the next few years it takes over many thinking tasks in many jobs: writing, checking, planning, buying, booking, coding and answering customers. Robots spread into hands-on work more slowly. Some jobs shrink, new ones appear, and lots of people have to change how they work. Most people still have work, and there is some time to adjust.

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: AI could write the maintenance accounts and check invoices before I open them. Robots may later scrub pools, but my screen work would change first.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: If this happened, what would you say about it at work, to friends, or online?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I would ask the partners to publish the number of wrong charges the new checker misses and the paid-hour plan. I would tell the contractor a fast invoice still needs a person to answer a dispute.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: And just between us, off the record, what do you really think it means for you?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: My own mid-level hours could shrink if one reviewer handles more contractors. Five months saved buys some time, but Cal's bus-driving wage alone would not carry the home loan and bills indefinitely.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: What would you actually do, starting now and in the first year after it arrives? Be as specific as you can.

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I would run a paid two-week comparison of anonymised maintenance accounts against signed job sheets only with Rosa's written approval. If it passes, I would learn the approved AI checker on paid time and use it on live work only after her written sign-off; if it fails or is refused, I would keep the authorised paid checks while offered. If my hours fall in the first year, I would take a posted accounts job only with written pay, hours and start date covering our home loan and bills after travel.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: How does it feel, picturing that?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I feel anxious about my paid hours, though I can help build an honest error log. A repeated filter charge is a small mistake that can lose a customer.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: Who checks the error log?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: Rosa and I would count missed duplicates and false cancellations against the signed sheets. We would put our names on the result before a live switch.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: Would you accept fewer hours at another firm?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: Only if the written wage after travel still pays the loan and food. A nearby office with no posted job is not a fallback I can spend.

I would keep a **named dispute answerer** for the contractor.
think: My own **mid-level hours** could fall with faster checks.
Cal's bus wage cannot replace my **typical accounting pay** indefinitely.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: AGI by 2028. Next one. The singularity hits fast. Within 2 years, by 2028, there is full AGI: artificial general intelligence, meaning AI that can do almost any thinking work a person can do, as well or better, and cheaper. Robots that can do hands-on work as well as people come about 3 years later, around 2031. It arrives before most companies, governments and families have time to prepare.

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: AGI in 2028 could match service sheets, spot charges and draft the return without my desk. Robots around 2031 would reach physical pool work later; those years do not postpone the account shock.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: If this happened, what would you say about it at work, to friends, or online?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I would ask the firm for written last-paid-day notice and severance terms. I would tell the contractor to keep signed service sheets while the software changes.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: And just between us, off the record, what do you really think it means for you?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I expect my accounting post to go when AGI handles nearly every invoice and tax schedule. Our five-month reserve helps, but a long gap would consume it, and I have been waking up thinking about the loan payment without my wage.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: What would you actually do, starting now and in the first year after it arrives? Be as specific as you can.

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: Now I would ask for written severance and keep every paid maintenance file offered. If my post ends in the first year after 2028, I would use the reserve for bills while seeking posted pool-supply store clerk roles, taking one only with written wage, hours and start date covering the home loan and food after travel, with duties I can safely do. Robots around 2031 may reach physical stock work too, so it would be a paid bridge.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: How does it feel, picturing that?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I feel alarmed by the likely loss of a familiar wage. The shelves in a pool-supply store do not promise me a job just because I know pool filters.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: Would the store hire an accountant?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: Only if an actual vacancy is posted and I can do the stock duties safely. I would not resign from paid accounts to ask around a counter.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: What if Cal gets overtime?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: We would count only overtime confirmed on his bus rota. I would not use a possible shift to justify taking lower written pay.

I would keep **signed service sheets** through the software change.
think: I expect my **accounting post** to end after 2028 AGI.

do: Request **written severance** and keep paid maintenance files only while offered.

Take a **posted store job** only with safe duties and written after-travel loan-and-food-covering wage, hours and start.
feel: I feel **alarmed** by expected wage loss.
S2.quote: The shelves in a pool-supply store do not promise me a job just because I know pool filters.
fieldNote: The **2028 desk loss** precedes physical pool-work robots; a stock job may only bridge until later automation.
An acceptable vacancy needs **safe duties** and written pay covering loan, food, travel and an actual start date.

steps.text: Request written severance; keep paid files while offered; after loss use reserve for bills
After 2028 loss take posted store job with safe duties written loan-food-travel-covering wage hours start

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: AGI by 2031. Now the same thing, a bit slower. Full AGI arrives within 5 years, by 2031: AI that can do almost any thinking work a person can do. Robots that can do hands-on work as well as people come about 3 years later, around 2034. There are a few years to see it coming, but it's still fast.

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: Five years gives me time to find out if a pool contractor would pay for someone to correct disputed service bills before AGI reaches accounts in 2031. Robots around 2034 are later for physical cleaning.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: If this happened, what would you say about it at work, to friends, or online?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I would ask the firm to post a paid service-correction role with a wage and supervised training. I would tell colleagues not to call a free pilot a new job.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: And just between us, off the record, what do you really think it means for you?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: The return fee might shrink, but I could learn to follow a customer complaint from the signed sheet to the corrected bill. I am experienced with accounts, not the person who repaired the pool, so the contractor must still check the technical facts.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: What would you actually do, starting now and in the first year after it arrives? Be as specific as you can.

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I would handle one disputed service bill monthly only if Rosa assigns paid time, supervises the correction and the contractor agrees to a billed service. I would keep paid accounts while offered; if the firm posts a correction-clerk role and pays its short course fee and study hours, I would enrol. Before or after 2031, I would take that posted job only with written wage, hours and start date covering our loan and food after travel; if account work ends first, I would use the reserve for bills during the search.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: How does it feel, picturing that?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I feel anxious about the accounts wage, but five years lets me see whether a real billed correction role appears. A complaint resolved for free is still free work.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: What if the contractor will not pay the fee?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I would stop the extra correction and keep the paid returns still assigned. I would not make a new job out of my evenings.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: Does that role avoid AGI?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: No, reading service records is thinking work too. A posted paid role would be a bridge, not an assurance it survives every tool.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: AGI by 2036. Last one. Full AGI arrives within 10 years, by 2036: AI that can do almost any thinking work a person can do. Robots that can do hands-on work as well as people come about 3 years later, around 2039. It's the same end point, but there's about a decade to prepare, change careers and make plans.

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: Ten years would put me at 68 when AGI reaches the tax desk in 2036. Robots around 2039 are later for physical maintenance; I cannot assume the accounts post lasts until then.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: If this happened, what would you say about it at work, to friends, or online?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I would ask the firm for its staffing dates and my retirement provider for a written income estimate. I would tell Cal we must check the home-loan balance before cutting any paid hours.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: And just between us, off the record, what do you really think it means for you?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I would like a shorter week eventually, but I do not know what income will replace my wage. Five months saved is helpful for a job gap, not proof I can fund years without earnings.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: What would you actually do, starting now and in the first year after it arrives? Be as specific as you can.

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I would ask the lender whether an extra forty from my monthly wage can reduce the home-loan principal without a penalty, only after our regular bills are paid; if it cannot, I would deposit forty as cash instead. I would keep paid maintenance accounts while offered and request a written retirement-income estimate before choosing a date to reduce hours. In the first year after 2036, if accounts end and verified income does not cover bills, I would use the reserve and take a posted accounts job only with written wage, hours and start date covering the loan and food after travel.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: How does it feel, picturing that?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I feel uneasy about the distant work change, but I can use the years to lower what we owe. A smaller loan would make a lower future wage easier to live on.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: Would you reduce hours before the loan is smaller?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: Only if a written shorter-hours offer and verified combined income cover the loan, food and travel. I will not treat a hoped-for pension as a paid shift.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: What if the lender charges a fee?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: Then I would put the forty into cash rather than pay to prepay the loan. I would check the regular payment and food first.

closing.speaker: interviewer
closing.text: Of the five pictures, which one worries you most, and what would actually help you if it happened?

closing.speaker: persona
closing.text: AGI by 2028 worries me most because the account wage could end before another paid role is posted. Written notice and a real vacancy with wages covering our home loan and food would let the five-month reserve do its job.

closing.speaker: interviewer
closing.text: Is there anything I didn't ask that I should have?

closing.speaker: persona
closing.text: You did not ask who pays when the contractor sends an invoice for a filter it never fitted. I can find a duplicate pool-filter charge, but someone has to be paid to correct it.

headlineQuote: I can find a duplicate pool-filter charge, but someone has to be paid to correct it.
portrait: Freya is a **58-year-old experienced mid-level accountant** with a bachelor's and professional qualification.
Her **typical pay**, five-month reserve and some nearby firms provide limited choices.
She uses AI **daily** but checks signed job sheets and requires paid testing before live changes.
She tests **billed service corrections** and pays extra on a home loan only when penalty-free.
biggestWorry: The **2028 AGI** case could end her wage before another posted role exists.
whatWouldHelp: She wants **written notice** and a posted job covering the home loan and food.
